stem: Calcium, magnesium and radium are Group 2 elements. Radium follows the same trends as the other members of Group 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify the highest energy orbital which contains electrons in a calcium atom. Sketch the shape of this orbital.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Write the equation for the thermal decomposition of calcium nitrate.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest which of the Group 2 nitrates, calcium, magnesium or radium, requires the highest temperature to decompose. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Predict what you would observe when aqueous radium chloride is added to aqueous sodium sulfate.
Do **not** refer to temperature changes in your answer.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
$^{25}_{12}\text{Mg}$ is an isotope of magnesium.

Determine the number of protons and neutrons in an atom of $^{25}_{12}\text{Mg}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: State the full electronic configuration of an atom of $^{25}_{12}\text{Mg}$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
A sample of magnesium contains three isotopes, $^{25}\text{Mg}$, $^{26}\text{Mg}$ and $\mathbf{X}$.

The percentage abundance of the three isotopes is shown in Table 1.1.

Table 1.1

| isotope of Mg | mass / a.m.u. | percentage abundance / % |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\mathbf{X}$ | {{blocked}} | 78.99 |
| $^{25}\text{Mg}$ | 24.99 | 10.00 |
| $^{26}\text{Mg}$ | 25.98 | 11.01 |

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text:
The relative atomic mass, $A_{\text{r}}$, is calculated by comparing the average mass of the isotopes of an element to the unified atomic mass unit.

Define the unified atomic mass unit.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the mass of $\mathbf{X}$. Use data from Table 1.1 and $A_{\text{r}}$ (magnesium) = 24.31 in your calculation. Show your working.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text: State **one** similarity and **one** difference in the properties of these isotopes of magnesium. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Magnesium, $\text{Mg}$, burns in oxygen, $\text{O}_{2}$.
The activation energy, $E_{\text{a}}$, for this reaction is $+148\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.text:
State **one** observation when magnesium burns in oxygen.
Do **not** refer to temperature changes in your answer.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 1.1:

- sketch a reaction pathway diagram for the reaction that occurs when $\text{Mg}$ burns in $\text{O}_{2}$
- label the diagram to show the enthalpy change, $\Delta H$, and the activation energy, $E_{\text{a}}$, for the reaction.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 1.1

parts.label: (g)
parts.text:
Cold water reacts slowly with a piece of $\text{Mg}$ to produce bubbles of $\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)}$.
Cold water reacts rapidly with burning $\text{Mg}$ to produce $\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)}$ in an explosive mixture.

$$\text{Mg} + 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_{2} + \text{H}_{2}$$

Explain why the rate of reaction of cold water with burning magnesium is greater.
